title: Corrective fix for B-8197dbad-subtask-review: Review Fix RecipesFolderStore .withSecurityScope iOS unavailability
description:
Blocked reason: saveBookmark (RecipesFolderStore.swift:55-68) calls startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() on line 55 but only calls stop on line 61 inside the do body. If url.bookmarkData() throws, the catch block runs clearBookmark() without calling stop — violating Apple's requirement to always balance start with stop. Fix: add `defer { url.stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() }` immediately after the start call (or after guarding on its return value), and remove the explicit stop on line 61.

Remaining work: Fix resource leak in saveBookmark: stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() must be called even when bookmarkData() throws (use defer). Optionally guard on the Bool return of startAccessingSecurityScopedResource().

handoff_summary.design_decisions: guard on the Bool return of startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() rather than discarding it with _ = keeps the API contract and avoids operating on a resource we didn't actually obtain access to. defer placed immediately after the guard ensures balanced cleanup regardless of which code path exits the function.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No new tests were added; existing tests in RecipesFolderStoreTests.swift cover the bookmark save/resolve flow. The tester agent should verify the defer path (throw case) is exercised.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: saveBookmark silently returns early (without saving) when startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() returns false. This matches the existing discard-pattern behavior and is appropriate for a corrective fix; escalating the error is out of scope.
